scope: CPU allocation pool controls, Win32 heap notifications and statistics, title memory diagnostics, and the exported history pointer on stock Proton.

controls: The normal PE loader ran the supplied xmem.dll and xcrdapi.dll with a test-only xbthunk.dll. The stand-in supplied the process heap, rejected partition handle requests and left notifications disconnected.

All 32 kind/size pairs matched the original default hysteresis. Setting one byte rounded to 4 MiB on every pair. The original returned 32 empty 32-byte statistics records with the caller DWORD at byte four preserved.
Original preallocation at zero hysteresis succeeded. A two-block request on the original DLL failed on Proton with error 87. The positive CPU commit lifecycle was exercised on TuxBox.

Original allocator tracking callbacks observed an allocation and its release. A five-byte dump buffer contained four X bytes and a NUL. The original reported tools memory unavailable. Its history pointer was null with the test-only partition provider.

implementation_controls: The guest requested two 4 MiB blocks, suballocated and wrote 256-byte and 512-byte aligned buffers, then reduced the hysteresis to zero. Statistics tracked both commits and decommits and preserved the high-water extent.

An 8 MiB Win32 allocation increased the queried heap commit. The allocation and free tracking callbacks received the process heap, flags, requested size and pointer. Clearing both hooks suppressed subsequent notifications.

The 4 KiB history mapping is read-only to its guest. Two successive 120-byte rows held host process counters without any intervening XMem call. A separate control unloaded the DLL near its half-second tick eight times and observed the history views released.

The free-page query wrote exactly seven words. A 512 MiB claim in the 64 KiB token pool reduced available ordinary backing, while the second set of node counters mirrored the first. Bounds and guards passed.

free_page_format.consumer: The packaged pixrt10.dll consumes all seven words.
free_page_format.kernel_control: Microsoft Windows 10.0.19041.329 x64 ntoskrnl.exe, SHA-256 9923b54ed79b57e1fd609b8226bac634d5167a1afcd0eb06bc79d1f1c274d496, MmManagePartitionNodeInformation. Its node accounting weights the four pair totals by 1, 16, 512 and 262144 ordinary 4 KiB pages. The Xbox DLL adds the 1 GiB class to the 2 MiB class in units of 512 and repeats the first node on a single-node configuration.

limits: Non-CPU preallocation, GPU-backed aliases and physical Xbox partitions are outside this checked profile.
The dump includes supported host counters. History covers the eight working-set rows, while Xbox allocator internals, error events and WER registration in later page fields remain unverified.
Tracking covers allocations and frees made through the XMem host heap path. Host Win32 realloc interception and cross-module notification remain open.
rerun: python build.py xmem && python tuxbox.py verify --only xmem --proton PROTON --prefix PREFIX --output build/xmem-check.json
